'*888888888'\\n ^'***'` 'YP' `~===*%'` ^'***'`\\n```\\n\\n\\\"Kinda like the original, but now for your terminal window!\\\"\\n\\nWolfentext3D is a simple take on a classic game with the following goals:\\n\\n* Lean and mean: all code should be contained in a single source file.\\n* Cross-platform: it should work reasonably well across Linux, Mac, and yes, even Windows.\\n* Instructive: the code should be clean, readable, and easy to follow.\\n* Stand-alone: No external dependencies, other than the Ruby core and standard libraries.\\n* No bitmap graphics: everything uses ASCII art and terminal colors!\\n\\nWolfentext is proudly (if not somewhat arbitrarily) written in pure Ruby.\\n\\nDocumentation may be derived from the code using the popular YARD documentation format.\\n\\nFeatures\\n========\\n\\n![Preview](preview.gif)\\n\\nHere are the features currently supported in Wolfentext:\\n\\n* Solid, orthogonal walls\\n* Recessed horizontal sliding doors\\n* Solid floor and ceiling background\\n* Textured floors and ceilings\\n* Collision detection with wall sliding\\n* Multi-directional pushwalls and moving walls\\n* Title, help, debug, and ending screens\\n* Over 16 colors of pixelated eye candy!\\n\\n...and here are some **missing** features that are still in the works:\\n\\n* [Stationary and usable objects](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/5)\\n* [Enemies and other entities](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/4)\\n* [Sounds and/or music](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/6)\\n* [Resizeable viewport](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/7)\\n* [Terminal type detection](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/8)\\n\\nRequirements\\n============\\n\\nThe only requirement for Wolfentext is a local installation of **Ruby 2.0.0+**.\\n\\nWolfentext should also work on all recent versions of OS X, Linux, and Windows. *(That said, Windows users may notice some issues when running Wolfentext in color mode. See the notes below for more information.)*\\n\\nInstallation\\n============\\n\\nTo install Wolfentext, simply download the `wolfentext.rb` file or clone the repo to your local machine:\\n\\n```\\n$ git clone http://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d.git\\n```\\n\\nUsage\\n=====\\n\\nTo start enjoying Wolfentext's pixelated goodness, command thine terminal thusly:\\n\\n```\\n$ cd wolfentext\\n$ ruby wolfentext.rb\\n```\\n\\nCompatibility\\n=============\\n\\nWolfentext has been tested against the following terminals and platforms:\\n\\n| Terminal | Platform | B/W performance | Color performance |\\n|----------------|--------------|----------------:|------------------:|\\n| Command Prompt | Windows 7 | 30-45 fps | 0-15 fps |\\n| ConEmu | Windows 7 | Not yet tested | Not yet tested |\\n| Cygwin | Windows 7 | Not yet tested | Not yet tested |\\n| GNOME Terminal | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 0-15 fps |\\n| Guake | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 45-60 fps |\\n| iTerm | Mac OS X | Not yet tested | Not yet tested |\\n| Konsole | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 45-60 fps |\\n| PowerShell | Windows 7 | 30-45 fps | 0-15 fps |\\n| Tilda | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 0-15 fps |\\n| tmux | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 45-60 fps |\\n| XTerm | Ubuntu 14.04 | 45-60 fps | 0-15 fps |\\n| Z shell (zsh) | Mac OS X | 45-60 fps | 45-60 fps |\\n\\nAlthough most modern terminal emulators seem capable of delivering playable frame rates, it goes without saying that users with integrated or low-end graphics cards may experienced decreased (and in some cases, unplayable) performance. I have noticed this myself when testing various terminal emulators on my main system: a 2010 HP Pavilion dv7 laptop with hybrid ATI graphics. *Some terminals performed over 100-200% faster when using the discrete ATI graphics card instead of the integrated Intel 915 chipset.*\\n\\n**If you are experiencing degraded or unplayable performance with Wolfentext in your favorite terminal program,** try adjusting the graphics properties of your host system (including switching to a discrete graphics mode, if your system supports it). Using the table above as a guide, you can also try running Wolfentext in another terminal emulator which may yield better performance.\\n\\nFinally, help us keep this table updated with the latest information! If you experience results different from these, please let us know by [filing an issue](http://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/) in the tracker.\\n\\nIssues\\n======\\n\\nDespite it's shimmering textiness, Wolfentext ain't perfect. Here are some known issues with the game of which you should be aware:\\n\\n* *Graphics*: In order to maintain code readability and cross-platform compatibility, Wolfentext uses a simple, single-buffered, terminal-based graphics system. In non-color mode, this should work quite well across all platforms, often achieving frame rates up to 60 fps. However, some users may notice **significant** performance issues when using *any* color mode in their preferred terminal (see Compatibility section above). Other third-party terminals may yield better performance but have not yet been tested.\\n\\n* *Input*: The input logic only handles one keypress at a time. Support for multiple keypresses is planned in a future release, assuming we can find a sensible cross-platform method that works.\\n\\n* *Terminal*: At present, the code assumes you are running this script in a compatible terminal. Logic should be added that detects not only the current terminal upon program start, but also what features are presently available to that terminal and whether they are compatible with the current version of Wolfentext.\\n\\n* *Optimizations*: Although the script utilizes several optimizations in key areas, the code could still benefit from (1) further graphical optimizations for common, low-performing terminal configurations; (2) reducing and/or eliminating the amount of floating-point math used across game calculations and lookup tables (with additional benchmarking to prove which optimizations are the most beneficial); and (3) optimizing any other remaining areas of the core ray casting engine, which presently consumes most of the processing time for each game loop iteration. Other areas of opportunity may also exist which have not yet been identified.\\n\\nAny suggestions for solving these issues are always welcome! See the Contributing section below.\\n\\nContributing\\n============\\n\\nPull requests that fix bugs or propose new functionality are always welcome, provided contributors keep the following conditions in mind:\\n\\n* Code contributions should be properly formatted and fully documented before final submissions are merged into master. If I make formatting changes to your code or request that you make similar changes yourself, please don't take it personally: the goal is to maintain a simple but consistent style across the entire project that is both readable and maintainable by others in the future. :-)\\n\\n* Before submitting new feature requests, it is recommended that you check the list of [open roadmap tickets](https://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/labels/roadmap) to see if anyone else is already working on that feature. This will help reduce the chance of duplicating efforts while allowing everyone to collaborate on the same feature more effectively.\\n\\n* All contributors whose pull requests are accepted will be given full credit for their ideas and/or submissions in the project README.\\n\\n* Since this project is officially [\\\"unlicensed\\\"](http://unlicense.org/) as public domain software, all contributors will need to agree to the following snippet and include it as a separate comment in their pull request before their contributions can be merged into the repository:\\n\\n```\\nI dedicate any and all copyright interest in this software to the\\npublic domain. I make this dedication for the benefit of the public at\\nlarge and to the detriment of my heirs and successors. I intend this\\ndedication to be an overt act of relinquishment in perpetuity of all\\npresent and future rights to this software under copyright law.\\n```\\n\\nIf you have any questions about this process, please let me know!\\n\\nSupport\\n=======\\n\\nIf you have any problems or suggestions, please let me know by [filing an issue](http://github.com/AtomicPair/wolfentext3d/issues/) in the tracker.\\n\\nHistory\\n=======\\n\\nWolfentext was originally born from the need to share a code sample with a potential recruiter. The sample had to be contained within a single file, and since I didn't have any public samples available at the time that I felt comfortable sharing, I spent the next few days creating the first iteration of Wolfentext from scratch. Since then, the script has taken on a life of it's own: adding new features, fixing bugs, and morphing into an homage to the classic 2.5D shooters from the days of my youth.\\n\\nFor the curious, here's a short summary table highlighting various milestones from past releases:\\n\\n| Release | Notable features |\\n|---------|-------------------------------------------------|\\n| 0.9.1 | Updated licensing and contributor information |\\n| 0.9.0 | Ceiling and floor textures |\\n| | In-game system messages |\\n| 0.8.0 | Wall textures |\\n| 0.7.0 | Multi-direction pushwalls |\\n| | Multi-direction moving walls |\\n| | Directionally colored walls (light/dark) |\\n| 0.6.0 | Sliding doors |\\n| 0.5.1 | Player strafing support |\\n| 0.3.0 | REAL non-blocking game loop and input system |\\n| 0.2.0 | Improved graphic system with almost no flicker |\\n| 0.1.0 | Initial alpha release |\\n\\nLicense\\n=======\\n\\nThis is free and unencumbered software released into the public domain.\\n\\nAnyone \",\"licenseIndicators\":[]},{\"id\":\"interactive-fiction-reference-043\",\"sourceGroup\":\"interactive-fiction-reference\",\"fileCounts\":{\".yml\":2,\"\":3,\".md\":1,\".c\":33,\".dat\":1,\".6\":1,\".h\":3,\".txt\":1},\"features\":[\"room\",\"story\"],\"readmeExcerpt\":\"```\\nWelcome to Dungeon. This version created 11-MAR-91.\\nYou are in an open field west of a big white house with a boarded front door.\\nThere is a small mailbox here.\\n>\\n```\\n\\n# DUNGEON (AKA Zork)\\n\\n**Public Domain Source Code for the Mainframe Game \\\"Dungeon\\\"**\\n\\nThis repository contains the Public Domain source code for *Dungeon*, the mainframe version of the game that served as the precursor to Infocom's commercial *Zork* trilogy.\\nThis codebase is a C port derived from the FORTRAN source of **Zork 2.6**.\\n\\n\\n## Installation\\n\\n### Fedora Linux\\n\\nThis package is available in the official Fedora Linux repositories.\\nYou can install it directly via the command-line:\\n\\n```bash\\nsudo dnf install zork\\n```\\n\\n### Building from Source\\n\\nTo build the game from the source files in this repository:\\n\\n```bash\\nmake\\n```\\n\\n\\n## Modern Maintainership & Philosophy (2013-12 to present)\\n\\n**Current Maintainers:**\\n\\n* Shane Thomas ([@devshane](https://github.com/devshane))\\n* Jan Dr\u00f6gehoff ([@Jan200101](https://github.com/Jan200101))\\n* Justin Wheeler ([@justwheel](https://github.com/justwheel))\\n\\n**Project Philosophy:**\\n\\nThis project utilizes the FORTRAN source of *Dungeon* (Zork 2.6) as its foundation.\\nThe primary design goal is code preservation.\\nWe aim to maintain the logic and behavior of the game as accurately as possible while updating the codebase to compile and run on modern C compilers and operating systems.\\n\\n\\n## History of the Implementation\\n\\nThis version of *Dungeon* has been modified from FORTRAN to C.\\nThe historical lineage of this code is as follows:\\n\\n1. **Original Development (MDL)**:\\n The original game (initially titled *Zork*) was written in the MDL programming language (MUDDLE) at the MIT Laboratory for Computer Science.\\n2. **PDP-11 Translation (FORTRAN)**:\\n Bob Supnik translated the MDL source into DEC FORTRAN for the PDP-11, renaming the game *Dungeon*.\\n3. **UNIX Port (f77)**:\\n The FORTRAN version was subsequently ported to `f77` for UNIX systems.\\n4. **C Translation**:\\n The C translation was generated from the `f77` version using `f2c`.\\n `f2c` is a FORTRAN-to-C translator written by David Gay (AT&T Bell Labs), Stu Feldman (Bellcore), Mark Maimone (Carnegie-Mellon University), and Norm Schryer (AT&T Bell Labs).\\n\\n*Note on Zork I:*\\nWhile often conflated, *Dungeon* differs from *Zork I*.\\n*Zork I* is a microcomputer adaptation comprising approximately one-third of the original mainframe game's map and puzzles.\\n*Dungeon* represents the more complete, albeit earlier, mainframe experience.\\n\\n### I. From original game documentation\\n\\nTo: Dungeon Players\\nFrom: \\\"The Translator\\\"\\nSubj: Game Information\\nDate: 8-OCT-80\\n\\n\\nThis is the first (and last) source release of the PDP-11 version of \\nDungeon.\\n\\nPlease note that Dungeon has been superceded by the game ZORK(tm).\\nThe following is an extract from the new product announcement for\\nZORK in the September, 1980 issue of the RT-11 SIG newsletter:\\n\\n \\\"'ZORK: The Great Underground Empire - Part I' ...was developed\\n by the original authors based on their ZORK (Dungeon) game for\\n the PDP-10. It features a greatly improved parser; command\\n input and transcript output files; SAVEs to any device and\\n file name; and adaptation to different terminal types,\\n including a status line on VT100s. Note: this is not the\\n FORTRAN version that has been available through DECUS. This\\n version has been completely rewritten to run efficiently on\\n small machines - up to 10 times as fast as the DECUS version.\\n\\n ...ZORK runs under RT-ll, HT-ll, or RSTS/E and requires as\\n little as 20K words of memory and a single floppy disk drive.\\n The game package, consisting of an RX01-format diskette and\\n an instruction booklet, is available from Infocom, Inc.,\\n P.O. Box 120, Kendall Station, Cambridge, Ma. 02142.\\\"\\n\\nZORK(tm) is a trademark of Infocom, Inc. It is available for several\\npopular personal computers as well as for the PDP-ll.\\n\\n### II. DEC FORTRAN to f77 Conversion (1981-11-17)\\n\\nThe conversion from DEC FORTRAN to Unix f77 was done by **Randy Dietrich, Lynn Cochran and Sig Peterson**.\\nMuch hacking was done to get it to fit in the limited address space of a PDP-11/44 (split I/D).\\nSuffice it to say that by leaving out the debugging package and not linking in the f77 i/o library, they managed to get it to run.\\n\\n### III. PDP to VAX (1985-12)\\n\\nBased on the work of Randy, Lynn and Sig, **Bill Randle** folded in the full save/restore functions and the game debugging package (gdt) into the PDP version to create a Vax/Unix version.\\nThis version also uses f77 i/o, thus eliminating the extra speak and listen processes needed on the PDP.\\n\\n### IV. Cleanup I (1986-12-11)\\n\\n**John Gilmore** (hoptoad!gnu) cleaned up the source files by moving most of the common declarations into include files and added comments from the original (_FORTRAN or MDL?_) source.\\nHis efforts are greatly appreciated.\\n\\n### V. Cleanup II (1987-02-09)\\n\\n**Bill Randle** added the PDP dependencies back into the Vax source files with `#ifdef`s in order to have just one set of sources.\\nPreviously, there were two sets of source: one for the PDP and one for the Vax.\\nIn addition, a shell escape of the form `!cmd` was added and the wizard can enter the gdt without having to recompile the source.\\nFinally, a man page was generated, based on the `dungeon.doc` file.\\n\\n### VI. f77 to C (1991-03-11)\\n\\n**Ian Lance Taylor** used the `f2c` translator to generate C source code.\\nThe resulting code was modified to remove the FORTRAN I/O library, to add simple more processing, and to change the format of the database file.\\n**Andre Srinivasan** helped test it.\\n**Jonathan Mark** made it work under MS-DOS and Microsoft C.\\n\",\"licenseIndicators\":[]}]}");

Noble in words, loyal to allies \u2014 yet always with an eye on personal legacy.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Strategist\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A long-game planner who treats rules, promises, and people as pieces. They are disciplined and effective, but will deceive, sacrifice allies, or reinterpret obligations to secure their own one Edge.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Knave\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Keeps just enough law to stay out of jail. A slippery operator who toes the line without any deeper loyalties.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Avenger\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Enforces personal justice like a holy wrathblade. Rules are tools, not ideals \u2014 they punish to feed their pride.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Mercenary\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A sword for hire who respects the structure of a contract only while it benefits them. Precise and professional, yet willing to exploit clauses, conceal risks, or betray the spirit of an agreement.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Marauder\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Wears structure like armor while carving a bloody path. Not cruel \u2014 just committed to their own violent climb.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Gladiator\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Upholds combat as ceremony. Respects tradition and fair fights \u2014 but glory and personal honor always come first.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Renegade\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Works with others when useful, then withholds truth or deserts commitments when the cost rises. Smart and efficient, but tolerated rather than trusted.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Drifter\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A wanderer with just enough charm to stay welcome. Avoids attachment but doesn't actively sabotage it.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Champion\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Fights for group causes \u2014 until the applause fades. Their heroism is real... but so is their thirst for praise.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Strategist\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Judges everything by personal outcome. Plans quietly, manipulates information, and treats ethical limits as obstacles rather than commitments.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Knave\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A wildcard with no compass. Acts on impulse or opportunity \u2014 sometimes helpful, often a headache.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Avenger\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Revenge is their religion. Morality isn\u2019t the goal \u2014 just evening the score, no matter who gets in the way.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Mercenary\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Coin, leverage, and survival come first. They may honor a deal when convenient, but will switch sides, hide terms, or exploit weakness if the reward is better.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Marauder\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Fights not for principle, but power. They don\u2019t pick sides \u2014 only targets.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Gladiator\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Honors the duel, not the war. Cares deeply about reputation and performance, not cause or creed.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Renegade\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A team-friendly anarchist until loyalty becomes inconvenient. They improvise brilliantly but lie, manipulate, or abandon allies without accepting the consequences.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Drifter\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A storm with a smile. Allies when it\u2019s fun, disappears when it\u2019s not. Hard to hate \u2014 but harder to trust.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Champion\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"A rebel hero \u2014 dramatic, bold, magnetic. Loyal in the moment, but always the star of their own tale.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Strategist\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"An unpredictable mastermind who plays every side. The dishonor lies not in improvisation, but in broken trust, concealed motives, and deliberate betrayal.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Knave\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Pure mischief incarnate. Chaos is its own reward \u2014 no loyalty, no plan, just vibes.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Avenger\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Burns worlds to avenge one wound. Justice isn\u2019t blind \u2014 it\u2019s furious.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Mercenary\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A volatile warrior for hire who treats promises as temporary. They may change sides mid-fight for better pay, greater thrill, or personal one Edge.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Marauder\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Wrecks, raids, and rages with zero remorse. No ideology \u2014 just destruction.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Gladiator\",\"profile\":\"Selfish \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Fights like it\u2019s performance art. Theatrics, blood, and brutal showdowns define them.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Operator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Works effectively inside institutions and teams, but manipulates procedure, hides costs, or uses allies as tools. Their public reliability masks a willingness to exploit trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Collaborator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A dependable participant in structured groups. They value order and teamwork, but are neither consistently self-sacrificing nor guided by a firm personal code. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Harmonizer\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Builds stable institutions, resolves conflict fairly, and keeps commitments even when compromise is difficult. Order and cooperation matter more than personal glory. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Adapter\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Uses rules and hierarchy as survival tools, changing loyalties or interpretations whenever one Edge demands it. They respect structure more than they respect trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Moderate\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Prefers order, proportion, and predictable procedure without strong altruistic or selfish pressure. Their personal code is situational rather than deeply fixed. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Ethicist\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Supports structure while judging each duty against a consistent inner code. They are neither especially selfless nor selfish, but they are principled and accountable. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Ravager\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Uses sanctioned force aggressively and treats legal authority as permission to intimidate, exploit surrender, or conceal misconduct. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Scoundrel\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A disciplined bruiser who accepts hierarchy and conflict but follows no dependable moral code beyond the rules currently in force. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Warrior\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Fights under rules of engagement, accepts consequences, and keeps their word. They may be confrontational, but their conduct remains principled. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Operator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A practical team player who gets results, but may hide costs, mislead partners, or discard commitments when efficiency demands it. Pragmatism alone is not dishonor; exploiting trust is.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Collaborator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Goes with the flow. A team member who supports without leading or resisting \u2014 blends in, stabilizes chaos.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Harmonizer\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Balances relationships with gancestry. A quiet peacemaker, not for recognition, but because harmony matters.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Adapter\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A survivalist who changes loyalties, stories, and standards to fit the moment. Flexibility becomes dishonor when they deny responsibility for promises made under earlier circumstances.\"},{\"name\":\"True Neutral\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Stands at the living center of all four axes. Their choices are situational, mixed, and not yet consistent enough to establish a strong direction. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Ethicist\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"A quiet moral compass. Doesn\u2019t preach, but always chooses the path that harms the fewest \u2014 even in stillness.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Ravager\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Uses violence as a tool and ethical limits as optional. Efficient and undramatic, but willing to exploit surrender, conceal intent, or strike without regard for accepted restraints.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Scoundrel\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A fighter without a cause. May brawl for coin, pride, or boredom \u2014 but rarely cares who wins the war.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Warrior\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Wields strength as its own code. Neutral in belief, yet bound by a personal oath of fair combat and protection.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Operator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Coordinates well through improvisation, but exploits goodwill, changes terms, or abandons shared commitments whenever freedom or one Edge calls. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Collaborator\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Works with others through spontaneity rather than structure. Helpful in the moment, but neither bound to a strong code nor driven by self-sacrifice. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Harmonizer\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Creates community without relying on institutions. They keep their word, respect people over systems, and resolve conflict through flexible but principled means. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Adapter\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Changes methods, identities, and loyalties rapidly, then denies obligations created by earlier choices. Their freedom is purchased with other people\u2019s trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Free Spirit\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Resists imposed structure and follows circumstance without a fixed altruistic, selfish, cooperative, combative, honorable, or dishonorable pattern. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Ethicist\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Rejects external authority while following a steady personal code. Their principles are chosen rather than imposed, and they accept the consequences of living by them. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Ravager\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Seeks confrontation without accepting restraint, accountability, or fair terms. Force and freedom matter more than promises or trust. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Scoundrel\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Competitive, unpredictable, and quick to escalate. They are not reliably cruel or principled; the moment decides which side appears. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Warrior\",\"profile\":\"Neutral \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Fights freely and rejects imposed rules, yet respects chosen limits, worthy opponents, and promises made in their own name. [Completed combination added in this merged edition.]\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Coordinator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"A mission-first organizer who brings order and aid to many, but cuts ethical corners, conceals costs, or sacrifices trust for results. Their altruism is genuine; their methods are not consistently honorable.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Mediator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A fair voice in the storm. Listens before acting, judges without ego, and restores peace without personal gain.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Guardian\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"The steadfast protector of the realm. Uplifts the weak, obeys the law, and inspires trust with every step.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Defender\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Protects others through disciplined systems, yet may deceive wards, break promises, or use coercive shortcuts in the name of safety. The goal is selfless, while the method compromises integrity.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Arbiter\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Seeks justice without bias. Mediates with detachment, but never loses sight of the greater good.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Sentinel\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"The silent watcher. Their loyalty is unwavering, their purpose pure \u2014 they serve to protect, not to be seen.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Enforcer\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Uses sanctioned force to preserve public order, but abuses procedure, withholds truth, or violates surrender when expedient. They may serve others while still acting dishonorably.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Vigilante\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Operates in shadows for the light. Defends the helpless but trusts fists over courts. A silent justice.\"},{\"name\":\"Lawful Crusader\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Lawful \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"A warrior of Architect duty. Law and mercy guide their blade. Fights not for conquest \u2014 but for righteousness.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Coordinator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Helps where needed and solves problems quickly, but may manipulate allies, conceal tradeoffs, or break commitments to keep the work moving. Useful and altruistic, not always trustworthy.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Mediator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A calming presence. Bridges gaps between factions, friends, and foes alike. Emotionally grounded and peaceful.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Guardian\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"The quiet heart of the group. Protects without ego, speaks with compassion, and walks the path of kindness.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Defender\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Prioritizes innocent lives over ideology, yet will lie, betray agreements, or use forbidden methods if convinced the outcome saves more people.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Arbiter\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A watcher of balance and need. Neither law-bound nor wild, this figure serves the people \u2014 however that must look.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Sentinel\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Honors a code of protection and patience. Acts when needed, guards without words, and never asks for praise.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Enforcer\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Takes the blows so others do not have to, but uses intimidation, deception, and excessive force without a stable code. Selfless purpose does not erase dishonorable methods.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Vigilante\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"Stalks the wicked to defend the helpless. Walks the line between justice and vengeance.\"},{\"name\":\"Neutral Crusader\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Champions the cause without borders. Fights for those who cannot, loyal only to their personal sense of good.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Coordinator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Builds shelters, rallies communities, and overturns harmful systems, but may manipulate supporters or break promises whenever a new plan seems more effective.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Mediator\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"The unconventional diplomat. Defuses tension with surprise hugs, strange jokes, or unexpected wisdom.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Guardian\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Cooperative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"A wild protector with a golden heart. Thinks laws are optional, but kindness is sacred.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Defender\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Creates safety through unexpected means, yet may deceive allies, violate trust, or ignore agreed limits in the rush to save lives.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Arbiter\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A whimsical judge of right and wrong. Morals fluid, heart steady \u2014 they fight for people, not systems.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Sentinel\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Neutral \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"Fights with passion and principle. Disregards rules \u2014 but never their personal honor.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Enforcer\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Dishonorable\",\"description\":\"Tears down barriers for the oppressed, but uses coercion, humiliation, or broken promises as routine tools. The cause is compassionate; the conduct is dishonorable.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Vigilante\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Neutral\",\"description\":\"A storm of justice. Protects others even when it means crossing lines, breaking rules, or being feared.\"},{\"name\":\"Chaotic Crusader\",\"profile\":\"Altruistic \u2014 Chaotic \u2014 Combative \u2014 Honorable\",\"description\":\"A freedom fighter wrapped in fire. Wields chaos in service of compassion. Unpredictable, unwavering.\"}],\"movement\":{\"minor\":\"25-100\",\"significant\":\"100-250\",\"major\":\"250-500\",\"campaign_defining\":\"800-1000\"},\"principles\":[\"Alignment records demonstrated behavior, not player worth.\",\"Continuity and coherent evolution earn equal XP.\",\"Alignment never removes levels, class features, or player authorship.\",\"Reputation, law, faction standing, and public rumor are separate tracks.\"]}");
